faults.fault: false absolute / a claim that fails in the real world
faults.finding: 'No charge crosses the gap', 'a steady voltage ... draws no more current' and 'once filled the capacitor draws no current' read alone in the dossier are false of a real capacitor, which leaks a trickle through its insulation.
faults.fix: Say 'in a healthy capacitor, next to none' and 'an ideal capacitor draws no more current; a real one leaks a trickle'.

faults.fault: the explanation skipping the causal step
faults.finding: 'the supply decides how fast the charge must arrive' skips the link: the supply's voltage fixes the charge at each instant, so how fast that voltage changes fixes how fast charge must arrive.
faults.fix: Spell out both halves of the step in one sentence.

faults.fault: the explanation skipping the causal step
faults.finding: 'fill to the same charge in half the time, so twice the current' gives the average, not why the peak doubles.
faults.fix: Add that every part of the wave is squeezed into half the time, so the voltage is twice as steep at each point and the current is twice as big at each point, its peak included.

faults.finding: 'Capacitor voltage at the cursor' is 31 characters, over the 30 allowed, and would wrap on a 340 px readout.
'motor run capacitors ... work the same way' is a plan detail not in RESEARCH and not needed.
faults.fix: Drop it; keep the long-cable link Dan already knows and the pointer to lesson 9.
